data.narrative:
Xtend is a Series B–stage defense and security company founded by Aviv Shapira that has raised $100M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 10 comparable companies—8 private firms and 2 public entities (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS)—all operating in the Defense & Security sector at similar stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $190M. Peer-median valuation across eight same-sector, same-stage private comparables produces $1.1B; the sample includes Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B), with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $162M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $658M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Xtend's positioning within the peer set. The gap between stage-progression ($190M) and peer-median ($1.1B) suggests the outcome hinges on whether Xtend's business quality, market traction, and defensibility track closer to the lower or mid-tier comparables. Key uncertainties include customer concentration, revenue trajectory, and technology differentiation relative to the peer cohort.
